resultados.refuerzo: Flying away is a different action from the one the text describes about the birds.
The north is a region; the population is concentrated on the coast and in the capital.
Chaparrón is a sudden, heavy shower that lasts only a short time.
Biblioteca is the library, where you borrow books for free and return them later.
After el aire you need a conjugated verb; mejorar is an infinitive and cannot go there.
Es is indicative; no creo que triggers the subjunctive, so sea is needed.
Será is future indicative; no creo que needs the present subjunctive sea.
Lack of jobs is a different cause; the correct answer is about holiday rentals raising prices.
Noisy souvenir shops is a complaint, not the cause the text gives for leaving.
Quejarse takes de: quejarse de que means to complain that something happens.
Failing exams is not the reason; the correct answer is about a family event and work.
Moving abroad is not the reason; the correct answer is about her father and having to work.
Resigning is not what colleagues asked; they asked her to wait.
Voting against is not what colleagues asked; the correct request was to wait.
After si in an imagined past, use hubiera plus the participle, not the conditional habría.
No creo que takes the subjunctive; tenga is the subjunctive form of tener.
Tendrá is future indicative; after no creo que the verb needs the subjunctive tenga.
Hablar is an infinitive; alguien que needs a conjugated verb, hable in the subjunctive.
Pero is common and simple in speech; the most formal connector here is no obstante.
Y eso que is informal and colloquial; no obstante is the formal choice.
The h in hola is silent; in Spanish the letter h is never pronounced.
The l is pronounced in hola; only the h is silent in this word.
The a is a vowel and is pronounced in hola; only the h is silent.
Perro means dog; the rr is a strong trilled sound, unlike the single r in pero.
Pero means but, not dog; a single r is a soft tap, so it is a different word.
Pelo means hair, a different word; the word for dog is spelled with rr.
C before e or i is a th in Spain and an s in much of Latin America; it varies.
C before e or i never sounds like English k; that is the hard c before a, o, u.
C before e or i is never silent; it always produces a sound in Spanish.
Hermana is the feminine form of hermano and keeps the h, with no accent mark.
Hermana has no accent mark; a tilde on the a would be wrong here.
Ermana drops the h; hermana keeps it, as Spanish spelling requires.
Café has a tilde because it is stressed on the last syllable, not the usual one.
Casa follows the usual stress rule, so it needs no written accent.
Libros follows the regular stress pattern, so it needs no written accent.
Qué with an accent marks a question word, as in an indirect question like I don't know what.
Que without accent is a relative or conjunction, not the question word in this sentence.
Qúe is not valid; the accent goes on the e, giving qué.
Canción ends in n with stress on the last syllable, so it needs the tilde.
Cancion lacks the tilde; words ending in n with final stress need one.
